consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning is Jesus Christ as the Lion of the tribe of Judah (royal/messianic power, majesty, victory, strength), with common alternatives for Satan as predatory devourer, God in judgment, hostile kingdoms/empires/rulers, and general courage; polyvalent and context-dependent.
book_summary: Lion as the devouring ruler or empire (beast-kingdom at its most royal and predatory: wicked rulers, princes as lions, Assyria/Babylon as lions that scatter the sheep); the figure’s rightful holder is the Lion of the tribe of Judah, and in His kingdom the lion is tamed.
consensus_core_identification: Christ as Lion of Judah (messianic royal power/victory)
book_core_identification: Devouring wicked ruler/empire (rightful holder: Christ as Lion of Judah; tamed in His kingdom)
boundary_disagreement: Book elevates the predatory empire/wicked-ruler sense (a consensus alternative) to definitional core while treating Christ as the rightful reclaimer plus taming motif; consensus treats Christ as primary and empires as secondary alternative. Shared referents retained but priority and emphasis reversed.
material_contradiction: None; both affirm Christological (Rev 5:5) and imperial/predatory (Prov 28:15; Jer 50:17; Ezek 19 etc.) uses without mutual exclusion.
rationale: Cores reduce to overlapping polyvalent royal-predatory agents (Christ + empires) already listed in consensus; book does not replace or deny the Christ referent but reweights the consensus alternative (devouring rulers/empires) as the entry’s leading identification and adds the taming note. This is a real boundary/priority shift (reclassification of what is central) without contradiction or novel referent, hence REFINED rather than MATCH or DIVERGENT.
strongest_objection: Consensus responses set Christ as primary_meaning with high confidence across all four; treating the empire sense as the main definition may understate the dominant Christological weighting.
